A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GIFT, with the same authors, the shared objective of generating fine-tuning residuals from pretrained weights, and retained FGVC/VTAB experiments. The text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original GIFT accuracy results on VTAB and FGVC in Tables 1–2, plus ImageNet clustering experiments and original qualitative analyses in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 reports original GIFT results on commonsense reasoning, FGVC, VTAB, and GLUE, together with architecture and component ablations in Tables 5–6. Attribution of some baseline scores to other papers does not change this assessment.

M1.justification: The main generator changes from v1's positional encoding and PaCa-based hyper-Transformer to v2's two bias-free linear layers, producing residuals omega·phi·psi. Visual interpretation uses omega·phi instead of learned PaCa assignments. Nonlinear networks become alternative parameterizations tested through ablations, substantially changing the proposed architecture and clustering mechanism.

E1.justification: v2 retains the 19 VTAB tasks and five FGVC datasets, adds eight Commonsense170k reasoning tasks and six GLUE tasks, and uses GSM8k for hyperparameter selection. v1's ImageNet downstream clustering experiment and multi-image mosaic scenario disappear. The revision therefore substantially changes evaluated domains and task coverage.

E2.justification: In the retained vision comparisons, v2 adds BitFit and removes TOAST and full fine-tuning; the FGVC linear-classifier baseline also disappears, while VPT and LoRA remain. New language comparisons include DoRA, LoReFT, VeRA, prefix tuning, adapter variants, and LoRA-FA (Tables 1 and 4), substantially expanding comparator membership.

E3.justification: Vision experiments switch from SGD to AdamW and use GIFT rank 16 and LoRA rank 8 instead of the earlier architecture dimensions and LoRA ranks. v2 uses only ImageNet-21k checkpoints, whereas v1 also tests ImageNet-1k and uses it for FGVC. Added language protocols include GSM8k-based tuning, six-epoch Commonsense170k training, and GLUE validation-set evaluation with task-specific metrics.

E4.justification: v2 Table 5 adds controlled comparisons of identity, sigmoid, GELU, MLP, Transformer, and MLP-Mixer parameterizations. Table 6 revises and extends the projection-layer comparison to both GIFT and LoRA against Q+V. v1's LoRA rank-sensitivity comparison, ImageNet clustering test, and appendix analyses of concept/class-specific clusters, mosaics, and cluster development during training are removed.

E5.justification: v1 reports no run counts or uncertainty estimates. v2 Appendix A specifies three-seed averages for commonsense reasoning and five-seed medians for GLUE, while Table 4 adds ± values for GIFT. These are newly reported practices, not an established increase over v1's run count. The meaning of the ± values and replacement seeds for unstable RoBERTa-Large runs remain unspecified.

E6.justification: v2 adds commonsense averages of 80.9, 82.6, and 86.7 for LLaMA-1/Llama-2/Llama-3, GLUE averages of 85.1 and 87.5, and resource and ablation results. FGVC changes from 89.3 in v1 to 89.39 in v2 under different pretrained checkpoints, architecture, and training, so this is not a same-setting gain. Individual VTAB scores and numerous appendix qualitative findings disappear.

T1.justification: v1's PaCa definitions and local residual-gradient argument are replaced by a factorized linear transformation formulation. v2 adds a derivation of parameter-space/activation-space equivalence (Equation 11), explicit shared multi-layer gradients (Equations 12–14), and a revised heatmap derivation. These are substantive mathematical changes rather than notation updates.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from a PaCa hyper-Transformer to shared linear adaptation with parameter/activation equivalence. The abstract and conclusion add language-task accuracy and parameter-efficiency claims, while describing GLUE performance as comparable. Earlier headline claims about proportional improvements with backbone strength and superior scaling with data complexity are dropped.

C2.justification: v2 introduces knowledge-preservation and simplicity arguments, hypotheses about nonlinear adaptation under distribution shift, and explicit limitations concerning manual cluster selection, inconsistent cluster responses, and unverified language localization. It removes v1's PaCa/predictive-coding explanation and discussions of spurious twig clusters and degraded mosaic classification. These substantially revise the interpretation and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix A revises the vision implementation guidance and adds language recipes covering learning rates, ranks, gradient accumulation, sequence lengths, and task-specific schedules in Tables 7–9. It identifies pyreft as the language implementation basis and timm as the vision checkpoint source. Reported hardware changes from RTX 8000/V100 to A100; the project's own code link remains.

R1.justification: v2 adds substantive positioning against DoRA, VeRA, and LoReFT, plus a neural-functionals subsection discussing equivariant weight-space networks and graph-based approaches. PaCa-ViT and predictive-coding references disappear. TOAST's paper remains cited for experimental splits but loses its central comparative role, substantially changing the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: The abstract, much of the introduction, approach, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around linear adaptation and language/vision applications. Related work moves from Section 2 to Section 5, contributions move into the introduction, and a dedicated limitations section is added. The appendix is reorganized around benchmark-specific implementation details, and the title drops 'Transformers'.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. The comparison diagram is redrawn, the detailed PaCa schematic and extensive visual appendix disappear, and an accuracy-versus-parameters plot and new cluster grids are introduced. Tables add resource columns, language comparisons, ablations, and hyperparameters; the VTAB display changes from individual tasks to category summaries.

improvement.justification: v1 lacks direct tests supporting its generator architecture and quantitative parameter/memory comparisons. v2 Tables 2–6 supply these, including vision baselines trained under matched settings, substantially strengthening the central design and efficiency arguments. Explicit derivations, repeated-run language experiments, and stated interpretability limitations further improve support and transparency. Removing detailed VTAB and visual analyses reduces completeness, and unspecified GLUE seed replacements weaken reproducibility, but these losses do not outweigh the stronger validation of the central method.
